        ((QuantumBlockEncoding.TensorTrainCanonical.complexCore A) * (QuantumBlockEncoding.TensorTrainCanonical.complexCore A).conjTranspose) =

gold.answer: P is true for arbitrary signed and unnormalized real f. The radicand is nonnegative, so m(f)(b)²=f(b,0)²+f(b,1)². Sum over prefixes. Every (n+1)-bit word is uniquely (b,v) with v∈{0,1}, and reindexing along this bijection yields N(m(f))=N(f). Therefore N(f)=1 propagates to the marginal whenever it is actually assumed, and the equality also preserves any other squared norm. This is a nonlinear length-table reduction; it does not retain signed amplitudes or itself specify a linear quantum evolution. A recursive preparation circuit uses additional signed splitting data to reconstruct them.

gold.answer: P is false. Take f=(1,0), g=(-1,0). Then f+g=(0,0), so m(f+g)=0, but m(f)=m(g)=1 and m(f)+m(g)=2. All values are exact; each of the two inputs separately has squared norm one. Thus norm preservation does not imply additivity or a linear isometry. The marginal loses sign information (m(-f)=m(f)); it is a nonlinear preprocessing map on amplitude descriptions. The correct source claim is squared-norm equality for each table, not linear evolution under addition. Even restricting to normalized inputs would not define a linear subspace; unit-norm inputs in this witness already expose the inappropriate linear-map claim.

  intro h
  let f : QuantumBlockEncoding.PrimitiveBasis 1 → ℝ := fun w => if w 0 = 0 then 1 else 0
